prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer looking down at a woven cot (charpoy) elevated above a flat ground plane (1.2 to 2.0 metres away in the upper-left background), with the wearer's own hands and turquoise knitting in the lower foreground at 0.3 to 0.4 metres. Within arm's reach (0.4 to 0.8 metres), a folded red garment rests on the left edge of the cot alongside the wearer's yellow-draped legs in the centre, while a second person sits immediately ahead and to the right on the same cot (0.7 to 1.2 metres away, about 0.3 metres from the wearer's feet), mostly cropped out of the right edge in frames 1–4. Across frames 1 to 4 the spatial layout stays nearly static as the wearer's hands move slightly, before the camera turns upward and rightward in frame 5, shifting the wearer's hands and red garment partly or fully out of the lower-left view and bringing the seated companion's upper torso (facing left with knees hugged, not looking at the wearer) and a third person seated on the ground behind them in red (1.5 to 2.0 metres away, facing left and smiling toward the left) into view. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the raised cot surface and overlapping limbs from the shadowed concrete floor below, and even captures the thin knitting needles and open weave of the cot. However, the map is unreliable along the top-right edge of frame 5 where the third person's head and torso merge into dark background depth values, and it flattens fine finger boundaries into smooth blobs.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map groups regions into discrete instances on the cot, separating the camera wearer's yellow-draped lower body (0.4 to 0.8 metres in front) from the adjacent companion's crossed legs and plaid-sleeved torso on the right (0.7 to 1.2 metres away, contacting the wearer's legs). In frames 1–4, the companion is heavily occluded by the right frame boundary, while in frame 5 the rightward head turn reveals the companion's torso angled to the left (within arm's reach of both the wearer and the third person behind them) and a tiny mask fragment at the top for the third person at 1.5 to 2.0 metres. Unlike the RGB image where yellow fabric, grey trousers, and shadows blend together along the cot, the instance masks delineate the boundary between the wearer's lap and the companion's legs in frames 1, 3, and 4. However, the segmentation is highly inconsistent and unreliable across time: in frame 2 it completely misses the wearer's lower body, hands, knitting, and the red garment on the left (at 0.5 metres), and in frame 5 it swaps mask colours while failing to segment the third person in red or the background utensils on the ground. Furthermore, the class labels are frequently misassigned or overlapping, labelling the folded red cloth as 'person' or 'backpack' and merging the wearer's hands and turquoise yarn into adjacent body masks.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates skeletal hand keypoints in magenta against an empty black background, tracking only the camera wearer's left hand at 0.3 to 0.4 metres in the lower-left foreground across frames 1 to 4. As the camera turns up and right in frame 5, the wearer's hands drop out of the lower frame and the map instead detects two hand skeletons at 0.8 to 1.3 metres in the upper right: the seated companion's left hand resting on their knee and the third person's right hand holding a phone near their chest. While this skeletal wireframe makes the exact finger curl, wrist orientation, and 3D articulation of the wearer's left hand and the distant phone-holding hand easier to read than in the cluttered RGB strip, it provides no information about scene layout or surface distances. The map is severely incomplete and unreliable for full-scene understanding because it fails to detect any yellow body skeletons for any of the three people across all five frames, leaving torso orientations and gaze directions completely unrepresented. It also misses the camera wearer's right hand (which is actively holding a knitting needle at 0.3 metres in frames 1–4, occluded slightly by the yarn) as well as the companion's right hand in frame 5.
